claims.text: Rapid solidification followed by mild annealing will refine the eutectic lamellar spacing to the sub-micron scale.
Refining eutectic lamellar spacing will impede dislocation motion and increase strength.
A uniformly fine eutectic microstructure will promote homogeneous plastic deformation and increase ductility.
Conventionally cast eutectic high-entropy alloys have relatively coarse lamellar or colony microstructures.
The baseline alloy has high strength from second-phase reinforcement but limited ductility because deformation is inhomogeneous.
Mild annealing after rapid solidification will relieve residual stresses without eliminating the desired refined microstructure.
Reducing interphase spacing limits dislocation pile-ups.
Limiting dislocation pile-ups through eutectic refinement increases yield strength via grain-boundary strengthening.
A uniform fine-scale phase distribution minimizes stress concentrations and delays micro-crack initiation.
Relative to the conventionally cast alloy, the rapid-solidified and annealed alloy will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength.
Relative to the conventionally cast alloy, the rapid-solidified and annealed alloy will have greater strain to failure or toughness.
The simultaneous strength and ductility improvement should hold when the constituent phases remain stable during rapid cooling and annealing does not induce undesirable transformations.
The intervention may be ineffective in alloys prone to amorphization or highly sensitive to residual stresses.
